hero.name: Sanghyeon Shin
hero.lead: A service planner who finds the answer in what users actually do, then builds and ships.
hero.summary: As a LIKELION intern I ran the [community platform](https://likelion.community/) used by 2,500+ students across 80 universities, and took **the 2,000-person national hackathon that registered through it from planning through the finals**. Inquiries the staff answered by hand for three hours a day, a submission check that would take about two days by hand, and finals results tallied in Excel — **I built an FAQ bot, a checking tool, and a finals console for them and ran them on site**.

about.description_1: I first got into IT through the frontend track of LIKELION's 12th cohort. Leading projects as staff for HUFS LIKELION's 13th cohort then taught me that **"who uses this, and why" has to be answered before "how do we build it."** Now, before I draw a screen, I check how users actually behave, and I build whatever is needed, **whether that's a screen, a backend, or an AI tool**.
about.description_2: I'm still improving RumiClean, a client project, after launch. I studied Global Business & Technology with an AI Convergence major and **won 11 awards** along the way.
about.training: SSAFY 15th cohort, Non-CS Java track, completed (Jan – Apr 2026)

principles.heading: How I work.
principles.to_projects: See how the three steps played out in the projects

items.t:
I find the problem
in what users actually do.
items.d: I start by watching how users and operators really move, and I re-check common assumptions against data. The point where people keep getting stuck becomes the problem the product has to solve.

items.t:
I turn that problem into a flow and rules,
and build it myself.
items.d: I design the user flow and the policy, and when needed I build it myself, from the screens to the backend and AI tooling, so it becomes a product that actually runs. Being able to check that it works as planned cuts the communication cost between planning and development.

items.t:
After launch, I watch users
and fix it again.
items.d: Launch is where user data starts coming in. I run the product where it's actually used and feed the questions and problems back into it.
